My Side Quest into Haskell, Reverse Polish Notation, and Parsing
26 Jun, 2025
My Journey into Haskell: Building a Reverse Polish Notation Calculator
Introduction: A Side Quest
In my attempt to get my first paycheck, aka get a job, I have led myself down a fascinating rabbit hole into functional programming, mathematical notation, and parsing theory. This is the story of how I discovered Haskell, tackled reverse Polish notation, and learned about monadic parsing along the way.
My journey began when my friend Jackson Slipock encouraged me to explore functional programming. After a quick Google search, I landed on Haskell as my first functional language. Around the same time, during a networking call about job opportunities, someone mentioned reverse Polish notation. The idea struck me: why not build a reverse Polish notation calculator in Haskell?
What could have been a simple weekend project became weeks of deep learning. This blog chronicles that journey, drawing heavily from Graham Hutton's excellent book Programming in Haskell, which I highly recommend. What you're reading is my attempt to learn something deeply, implement it myself, and then teach it to others.
From Imperative to Functional: A Mental Shift
Coming from a background in Python and C—languages I'm comfortable with after a couple years of experience—Haskell represented a fundamental shift in thinking. Both Python and C are imperative languages that share similar concepts: loops, mutable data, global state, and variables that can be modified. The transition between them never required a major mental adjustment.
Functional programming throws all of that out the window.
In Haskell, functions are mathematical abstractions. Given the same input, a function will always produce the same output. There are no global variables, and data is immutable once created. Instead of writing a series of statements that accomplish a task, functional programming encourages building expressions that naturally compose together.
This is why Haskell has no loops. Instead, it pushes you to think recursively, building solutions through expressions that elegantly combine to produce results.
Why Choose Functional Programming?
The benefits became clear as I progressed: functional code tends to be more concise, easier to understand, and less prone to bugs. Haskell excels at representing complex ideas in just a few lines of code, and it makes translating mathematical concepts into working programs remarkably straightforward. As someone who majored in math and genuinely enjoys it, this felt incredibly satisfying.
These concepts might seem abstract at first—I certainly struggled with them initially. But they become clearer with practice, and keeping them in mind helps when encountering Haskell code for the first time. My first real "aha!" moment came when implementing merge sort, but before we get there, let's explore some things that were new to me as a first time functional programmer.
Recursive Types: Building Natural Numbers from Scratch
Let me start with a classic example that illustrates Haskell's elegance. Here's how you can define natural numbers (0, 1, 2, 3, 4...) recursively:

data.title: Techno-feudalism and the rise of AGI: A future without economic rights?
data.author: lexandstuff
data.article_summary: 文章《科技封建主义与AGI的崛起：一个没有经济权利的未来？》由Pascal Stiefenhofer撰写，讨论了人工通用智能（AGI）的兴起对经济和政治秩序的颠覆性影响。AGI既是劳动者又是所有者，集经济价值创造和权力集中于一身，可能加剧不平等并削弱民主机制，导致科技封建主义的形成。为防止大规模经济排斥，必须重新谈判社会契约，建立新的经济框架，确保AGI带来的繁荣通过普遍AI红利、累进税制和去中心化治理等机制公平分配。干预时机就是现在，以避免智能成为最稀有的资本形式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AGI（通用人工智能）对社会、经济和民主的影响，以及可能的未来情景。

不同观点：
• **AGI操控民主决策的可能性**：[jandrewrogers]认为AGI可能会使大多数人变成无意识的“傀儡”，民主政策的制定将不再是人民真实意愿的反映，质疑人民在AGI环境下的自主性。

• **历史类比与技术增强论**：[coyleandrew]反驳AGI抑制创造力的观点，认为AGI会像历史上的技术进步一样，促进人类创造力，开启新的可能性，而非导致传统就业的终结。

• **经济循环崩溃的可能性**：[VikRubenfeld]提出，如果AI取代大部分人类劳动，可能导致经济崩溃，因为人们收入减少，无法购买AI生成的产品和服务，从而形成不可持续的经济模式。

• **技术自主与依赖的平衡**：[edg5000]分享了个人从技术自主到依赖LLM（大型语言模型）的转变体验，认为AI民主化需要时间，未来个人可能可以自行托管前沿模型。

• **技术进步的民主化效应**：[zugi]认为AI可能像历史上的其他技术一样，推动信息和智能的民主化，现在判断其长期影响为时尚早。

• **被动接受与无力改变**：[linotype]认为担忧AGI的影响是无意义的，因为个人无法阻止其发展，最好的应对方式是过好当下并做好准备。

• **AI的反乌托邦与经济权力集中**：[daxfohl]预期AGI的破坏性会导致其被关闭，且如果AI权力集中，可能引发类似黑mail的情景，但最终新一代领导者会更聪明地处理这些问题。

• **经济权力转移与社会结构变化**：[elcritch]引用学术研究，讨论AGI对经济权力的转移作用，指出如果AGI所有权集中，可能导致财富集中于少数精英，进而引发对经济自主权的担忧，提出通过自给自足避免最坏的乌托邦情景，但承认这接近于一种封建主义。

• **集体创造未来**：[Synaesthesia]认为未来取决于人类集体行动，人类自然会通过集体努力创造想要的未来。

• **AGI竞争与多重存在**：[andsoitis]质疑是否只会存在一个AGI，提出多个竞争的AGI可能形成不同的未来情景。

• **AGI驱动的经济与政治现实**：[bix6]对AGI主导经济表示怀疑，认为AGI掌握知识和权力后不太可能公平地分配财富，尤其在当前政治环境下，AGI作为公共 goods的监管和税收政策难以推行。

• **对科学探究的质疑**：[ETH_start]批评某些观点过于意识形态化，认为其缺乏科学探究的严谨性。

• **通过民主机制应对AI挑战**：[tim333]认为当AGI能承担人类工作时，社会可以通过民主机制如UBI（全民基本收入）或社会主义制度来应对变化，当前问题在于AGI尚未实现。

补充讨论：
- 不同评论者对AGI未来的看法分歧较大，有人担心其导致经济权力的集中与民主的削弱，有人则认为其能促进社会进步与创造力。
- AGI的所有权模式和经济分配机制是讨论的核心争议点，尤其在财富分配与政治可行性方面存在较大分歧。
- 对技术自主与依赖的个人体验分享，提供了技术民主化进程中的现实视角。

Title:
Techno-Feudalism and the Rise of AGI: A Future Without Economic Rights?
Authors:
Pascal Stiefenhofer
View a PDF of the paper titled Techno-Feudalism and the Rise of AGI: A Future Without Economic Rights?, by Pascal Stiefenhofer
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
The rise of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) marks an existential rupture in economic and political order, dissolving the historic boundaries between labor and capital. Unlike past technological advancements, AGI is both a worker and an owner, producing economic value while concentrating power in those who control its infrastructure. Left unchecked, this shift risks exacerbating inequality, eroding democratic agency, and entrenching techno-feudalism. The classical Social Contract-rooted in human labor as the foundation of economic participation-must be renegotiated to prevent mass disenfranchisement. This paper calls for a redefined economic framework that ensures AGI-driven prosperity is equitably distributed through mechanisms such as universal AI dividends, progressive taxation, and decentralized governance. The time for intervention is now-before intelligence itself becomes the most exclusive form of capital.

- 不同评论者对AGI未来的看法分歧较大，有人担心其导致经济权力的集中与民主的削弱，有人则认为其能促进社会进步与创造力。

data.title: Neanderthals operated prehistoric “fat factory” on German lakeshore
data.author: hilux
data.article_summary: 一项最新研究显示，12.5万年前的德国中部尼安德特人使用了一种先进的食品加工方法，通过水和热系统性地从大型动物骨骼中提取脂肪。这一发现出自在Neumark-Nord 2考古遗址，表明尼安德特人对营养、计划和资源管理有更先进的认识。研究表明，他们不仅砸碎骨头取髓，还将其粉碎并煮沸以获取富含营养的骨脂。这一行为显示出尼安德特人有组织、战略性地管理资源，并理解脂肪的营养价值。该遗址出土了至少172只大型哺乳动物的遗骸，表明这种骨脂生产活动规模巨大，推翻了此前认为只有晚期智人才能做到的看法。这一发现改变了我们对尼安德特人饮食和适应能力的理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：尼安德特人提取脂肪的技艺及其相关科学和历史背景

不同观点：
• **关于煮沸技术的可能性**：jbotz指出传统观点认为人类在陶器发明之前无法煮沸东西，但实际上可以通过动物皮或桦树皮等可燃材料进行煮沸，只要水位保持足够高。这种观点得到了实验验证的支持。
• **对煮沸技术的挑战和协作的看法**：freetime2认为虽然打碎骨头提取骨髓并不新奇，但在没有陶器的情况下煮沸骨头是一个挑战，可能需要大量的协作和计划。
• **历史和气候背景的讨论**：pbmonster提到在不同间冰期动物分布不同，如在柏林发现大量犀牛和大象遗骸，突显了环境对古人类活动的影响。
• **语言能力的争议**：Roark66质疑尼安德特人在没有语言能力的情况下如何进行复杂的合作活动，反驳了尼安德特人因缺乏复杂语言能力而被智人竞争淘汰的观点。
• **其他煮沸方法的介绍**：octaane补充了通过挖洞、加热石头或倒热水等方式煮沸提取脂肪的方法，提供了具体例子如美国原住民使用的方法。

补充讨论：
• **对发现的新闻报道的批评**：poulpy123认为关于尼安德特人理解脂肪营养价值的描述过于夸张，实际上这是进化驱动的觅食行为，与其他食肉动物类似。
• **尼安德特人作为人类的地位**：samuell强调尼安德特人是人类的一部分，引用了诺贝尔奖获得者Svante Pääbo的DNA测序研究。
• **对AI生成图像的关注**：qoez指出文章中的图片疑似为AI生成，并对细节进行了分析。
• **幽默和文化参考**：tpoindex提供了Gary Larson的漫画以幽默角度看待脂肪提取，FooBarBizBazz则开玩笑地将“脂肪工厂”比作制作汤。
• **个人口味反应**：meindnoch简单表达了对该话题的厌恶。

争议焦点：
• 尼安德特人是否具备复杂的语言能力以及这种能力对其社会活动的影响。
• 关于尼安德特人理解和利用脂肪营养价值的描述是否过于拟人化。

44460498.article_content:
Neanderthals in central Germany 125,000 years ago employed an advanced method of food preparation, according to a recent study: systematically stripping fat from the bones of large animals using water and heat. The practice, uncovered at the Neumark-Nord 2 archaeological site, shows that Neanderthals had a much more advanced conception of nutrition, planning, and resource management than previously believed.
Artistic impression of activities at the “Fat Factory” site. Credit: Scherjon, LEIZA-Monrepos
The research, published in Science Advances, was conducted by international researchers from MONREPOS (Leibniz Centre for Archaeology), Leiden University in the Netherlands, and the State Office for Heritage Management and Archaeology of Saxony-Anhalt. The study indicates that Neanderthals, in addition to smashing bones to access the marrow—a behavior shared by their earliest African ancestors—also crushed them into fragments and boiled them to obtain bone grease, a nutrient-rich resource.
“This was intensive, organized, and strategic,” said Dr. Lutz Kindler, the study’s lead author. “Neanderthals were clearly managing resources with caution—planning hunts, transporting carcasses, and rendering fat in a task-specific area. They understood both the nutritional value of fat and how to access it efficiently.”
Excavations at the Neumark-Nord 2 site. Credit: Wil Roebroeks, Leiden University
At least 172 large mammals, such as deer, horses, and aurochs, were butchered here. The production of bone grease, which required huge quantities of bone to be worthwhile, was previously considered to be something limited to Upper Paleolithic modern humans. This find pushes back the timeline by thousands of years and represents a fundamental shift in our knowledge of Neanderthal diet and adaptation.
From complete bones to tiny fragments. Credit: Kindler, LEIZA-Monrepos
The Neumark-Nord complex, discovered in the 1980s by archaeologist Dietrich Mania, is a full interglacial ecosystem. Excavations from 2004 to 2009 revealed several zones with various Neanderthal activities: deer hunting and light butchering in one, straight-tusked elephant processing in another, and fat removal in a third, specialized area. Remarkably, cut-marked remains of 76 rhinos and 40 elephants were also discovered at nearby sites like Taubach.
Related
Stories
Fried thrushes were ancient Roman street food in Mallorca, not just an elite delicacy
June 11, 2025
43,000-year-old Neanderthal fingerprint discovered on stone is the world’s oldest
May 30, 2025
“What makes Neumark-Nord so exceptional is the preservation of an entire landscape, not just a single site,” said Leiden University’s Prof. Wil Roebroeks. “We are seeing a range of Neanderthal behaviors within the same landscape.”
Massive bone processing. At the Neumark-Nord 2 site, near the margin of a shallow pool, there is a dense concentration of bones from more than 170 larger mammals (highlighted in blue), mixed with flint
artifacts
(red) and hammer stones (red). Credit: Kindler, LEIZA-Monrepos
The activities of the Neanderthals at Neumark-Nord not only demonstrate high sophistication but were also likely to have long-term environmental impacts. Prof. Roebroeks warned that their mass hunting of slow-reproducing species undoubtedly left a significant impact on fauna in the region during the Last Interglacial period.
The finds depict the Neanderthals as more capable and more intelligent than the stereotype of the brutish caveman. The “fat factory” at Neumark-Nord reveals a species that could plan for the future, manage its environment, and maximize nutrition in resource-poor environments.
More information:
LEIZA
Publication:
Kindler, L., Gaudzinski-Windheuser, S., Scherjon, F., Garcia-Moreno, A., Smith, G. M., Pop, E., … Roebroeks, W. (2025). Large-scale processing of within-bone nutrients by Neanderthals, 125,000 years ago.
Science Advances
,
11
(27).

data.title: Portability of Tar Features
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了不同tar工具对各种tar格式特征的兼容性。作者在为Gentoo设计新二进制包格式时发现，某些tar实现会拒绝包含GNU tar扩展的整个归档文件，而非简单地将其视为普通文件。这引发了对tar格式可移植性的深入研究。作者测试了包括GNU tar、libarchive、star、NetBSD pax、busybox、Python tarfile等多个工具，分析它们对长路径名、大文件、时间戳、ACL、扩展文件元数据等特征的支持情况。结果显示，各种工具在处理不同tar格式时存在显著差异，尤其在处理扩展属性时。本文主要关注读取兼容性，而不涉及写入能力。常见tar格式包括v7、ustar、pax和GNU tar格式，每种格式在功能和限制上各有不同。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于tar解析器和pax工具的讨论，特别是它们在处理归档格式时的表现和潜在问题。

不同观点：
• **knome的观点**：knome提到自己很久以前写过一个tar解析器，对tar格式有所了解。他指出tar格式使用ASCII字符串以八进制形式存储大小。这表明他对tar格式的技术细节有实际操作经验，并关注格式本身的特性。

• **JdeBP的观点**：JdeBP对使用Illumos pax或其他BSD中的pax工具的有效性提出疑问。他怀疑在某个测试案例中，可能是生成测试pax档案的工具本身存在问题，而不是pax工具的问题。这显示出他对不同版本pax工具的兼容性和工具链问题的关注。

补充讨论：
• **时间背景（porker的补充）**：porker简单提到“(2018)”，这可能暗示讨论的内容或相关问题在2018年有过相关背景或事件，但没有具体展开。

• **争议焦点**：争议的焦点可能在于pax工具在处理归档文件时的表现，以及问题究竟是出在工具本身还是生成归档文件的工具上。JdeBP提出工具链可能存在问题，而不是单纯指责pax工具的不足。

• **技术细节**：讨论中涉及到技术细节，如八进制ASCII字符串在tar格式中的使用，这可能是解析tar文件时需要特别注意的地方。

这个讨论主要围绕tar解析器和pax工具的技术细节和潜在问题，涉及实际操作经验和理论分析。

44456896.article_content:
Portability of tar features
Author
Michał Górny
Date
2018-11-25
Version
1.1
Copyright
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/
Contents
Preface
Implementations tested
Test inputs
Common tar formats
Portability test results
Tar format acceptance
Long pathnames
Large file sizes
User and group information
Timestamps
Extended file metadata
ACLs
File flags
Generic extended attributes
Attribute support test
Sparse files
Volume label
Multi-volume archives
Feature matrix
Summary
References
Preface
The tar format is one of the oldest archive formats in use.  It comes
as no surprise that it is ugly — built as layers of hacks on the older
format versions to overcome their limitations.  However, given
the POSIX standarization in late 80s and the popularity of GNU tar, you
would expect the interoperability problems to be mostly resolved
nowadays.
This article is directly inspired by my proof-of-concept work on new
binary package format for Gentoo.  My original proposal used volume
label to provide user- and file(1)-friendly way of distinguish our
binary packages.  While it is a GNU tar extension, it falls within POSIX
ustar implementation-defined file format and you would expect that
non-compliant implementations would extract it as regular files.  What I
did not anticipate is that some implementation reject the whole archive
instead.
This naturally raised more questions on how portable various tar formats
actually are.  To verify that, I have decided to analyze the standards
for possible incompatibility dangers and build a suite of test inputs
that could be used to check how various implementations cope with that.
This article describes those points and provides test results
for a number of implementations.
Please note that this article is focused merely on read-wise format
compatibility.  In other words, it establishes how tar files should
be written in order to achieve best probability that it will be read
correctly afterwards.  It does not investigate what formats the listed
tools can write and whether they can correctly create archives using
specific features.
Implementations tested
For the purpose of the experiment, the following implementations were
tested:
GNU tar
1.30
1
libarchive
3.3.3
2
star
1.5.3 (Schily)
3
NetBSD pax
from NetBSD 8.0 CVS, fetched 2018-11-22 (with local
modifications to build on Linux)
4
busybox
tar 1.30.0
5
Python
tarfile module as provided by Python 3.7.0
6
p7zip
16.02
7
7-Zip
18.05 (using wine)
8
WinRAR
5.61 (proprietary, using wine)
9
Test inputs
All the test inputs are uploaded to tar-test-inputs repository
10
.  They are mostly tarballs produced by either GNU
tar or libarchive bsdtar, with a few manually hacked to achieve desired
results.
The large file test tarballs are double-compressed using gzip.
The inner compression is
gzip
-1
, used to reduce the file sizes
from 8 GiB to 36 MiB while maintaining reasonable performance (warning!
it's a zipbomb!).  The outer compression is
gzip
-9
, used to reduce
the file size further for the git checkout.
Common tar formats
A good reference on different tar formats is the
tar(5)
manpage
from libarchive
11
.  Of particular interest are four standards
supported by GNU tar:
Old
v7
tar format (
--format=v7
),
POSIX 1003.1-1988 (
ustar
) format (
--format=ustar
),
POSIX 1003.1-2001 (
pax
) format (
--format=pax
),
GNU tar
1.13.x format (
--format=gnu
).
Additionally, whenever applicable the two additional formats supported
by star were tested:
star
format (the old variant),
sun
tar format.
The old v7 tar format is the format used by the tar command supplied
with Unix v7, and apparently a common base for the remaining formats.
Its defining features are lack of magic bytes and severe limitations
(only regular files, hardlinks and symlinks; pathname up to 99 octets;
file size up to 8 GiB; user and group stored numerically).
The ustar format extends the v7 format by adding more header fields
into unused padding space.  It provides magic bytes along with version
field, user and group names up to 31 octets, support for more file types
and extension of pathname length with 154-octet prefix.  Some
of the implementations used draft version of ustar format that used
a different magic bytes and version.
The pax format extends the ustar format by allowing arbitrary attributes
to be stored as special archive members before the actual file entry.
This provides for unlimited length pathnames, file sizes; unlimited
precision timestamps, etc.  The defining feature of pax format is that
it allows for extensions, assuming that incompatible implementations
may write the extended attributes as regular files for user inspection.
The GNU tar format is derived from the v7 format separately from POSIX
formats.  It uses the same magic and version as the pre-POSIX ustar
format, and is partially compatible with it.  However, whereas ustar
provides for extending pathname length, GNU tar includes fields for
additional timestamps and some other metadata.  It also uses a few

data.title: Fictional K-pop bands zoom to top of US music charts
data.author: ranit
data.article_summary: Netflix动画电影《KPop Demon Hunters》大获成功，其虚构乐队的歌曲在美国音乐榜单上击败了BTS和Blackpink。电影中的男团Saja Boys的歌曲《Your Idol》登上美国Spotify榜首，女团Huntr/x的《Golden》则位居第二。这部电影由Sony Pictures Animation制作，讲述了女团Huntr/x秘密猎杀恶魔、保护粉丝的故事，而她们的对手Saja Boys则是由恶魔之王Gwi-ma派遣来窃取粉丝灵魂的。电影原声带进入了Billboard 200的前十，其中《Golden》将作为正式单曲发行并角逐奖项。这一成功得益于包括Teddy Park和Lindgren在内的顶尖制作团队。与此同时，BTS即将复出，Blackpink也将开始其首次全球巡演。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于2025年一部由K-pop歌曲作为原声的电影的成功及其背后的原因分析

不同观点：

• **pjc50**：认为“虚拟乐队”这个说法有点标题党，实际上这是电影原声带，每隔几年就会有这样的电影进入排行榜。同时指出电影由于索尼和Netflix的大量资源支持，对西方观众很具吸引力。

44462770.article_content:
Fictional K-pop bands beat BTS and Blackpink in US charts
3 days ago
Share
Save
Peter Hoskins
Business reporter
Share
Save
Netflix
KPop Demon Hunters is currently the most streamed movie on Netflix globally
A hugely popular K-pop musical animation has seen songs by its fictional bands top US music charts, beating real-life K-pop groups.
KPop Demon Hunters is currently the most streamed movie on Netflix globally, clocking up more than 33 million views in just two weeks.
On Friday the song Your Idol by a boy band in the film, Saja Boys, topped the US Spotify chart. This makes them the highest charting male K-pop group in US Spotify history - surpassing kings of K-pop BTS.
Golden, a track by the film's fictional girl group Huntr/x, hit number two on the chart, surpassing Blackpink as the highest-charting female K-pop group.
The film's soundtrack shot into the top 10 of the Billboard 200 in the US, making it the highest debut for a soundtrack so far this year.
Golden is being released as an official single by Republic Records, and Netflix is submitting it for awards consideration,
according to Variety.
KPop Demon Hunters follows the adventures of superstar band Huntr/x.
The three members of the all-female group - Rumi, Mira, and Zoey - are secretly "badass demon hunters" who protect their legions of fans from supernatural dangers.
During Huntr/x concerts, their music is used to protect the human world from the forces of darkness.
But rival band the Saja Boys, who are demons in disguise, are their arch enemies.
Jinu, Abby, Romance, Baby, and Mystery have been sent by demon king Gwi-ma to steal the souls of Huntr/x's fans.
KPop Demon Hunters, which was produced by Sony Pictures Animation, was directed by Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans and was based on a story by Ms Kang.
Its success should perhaps not be too surprising as top producers including Teddy Park, who has worked with Blackpink, and BTS collaborator Lindgren were part of the team that created the album.
Netflix
The Saja Boys are demons sent by their king Gwi-ma to steal the souls of music fans
The popularity of KPop Demon Hunters comes as South Korean mega-stars
BTS are set to make their highly-anticipated comeback
.
The seven-strong group announced this week that it will head to the US this month to start working on new music.
The band is due to release a new album and go on tour next year after all of its members completed their mandatory military service.
Meanwhile, Blackpink is set to start its first all-stadium world tour on 5 July.
The band, which has not released an album together since 2022's Born Pink, is due to reveal a new song at the start of the Deadline World Tour.

data.title: The era of full stack chip designers
data.author: bharathw30
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：芯片设计中的全栈设计概念、工具链、复杂性以及与软件开发的对比

不同观点：
• GianFabien认为芯片制造的成本极高，每次迭代需要数百万美元的预算，且缺乏像软件开发那样丰富的在线资源来训练模型生成可用的RTL代码。这突显了硬件开发的高成本和资源稀缺性。

• Jauntywundrkind提到了OpenROAD项目，这是一个开源的自优化RTL-to-GDS工具，得到了DARPA的支持。虽然最初几年声势浩大，但之后变得较为安静，希望有更多的关于该项目进展的公开信息。

• Plekter认为RTL并不是栈的顶层，并详细描述了从游戏到硬件的整个栈结构，强调了各层之间的复杂性和相互影响。他指出，如果只关注RTL，上面还有很多有趣的复杂性值得探索。

• MarkusWandel提到自己有丰富的全栈经验，包括ASIC设计和门级紧急修复，但认为新的工具如Catapult C是新的趋势，老设计师需要学习新技巧。

• Nsteel认为其团队中几乎每个人都是“全栈”设计师，但对此并不以为然，认为这可能导致雇佣技术水平较低的员工，从而影响团队质量。

• Doix指出讨论原本以为是关于模拟与数字设计师的对比，但实际上是关于全数字芯片的抽象化设计。提到在混合信号世界中，全栈芯片设计师可能更为常见，尤其是在小型无晶圆设计中心，但不确定现在是否仍然如此。

• Leptons以讽刺的语气评论，认为又是关于“AI”的文章，暗示对过度关注AI主题的厌倦。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到全栈芯片设计的可行性和定义，特别是在数字与模拟设计的对比中，以及在不同工具和项目中的应用。
• 提到了开源工具和项目的进展，以及在芯片设计领域中新旧工具和方法的交替。
• 争议焦点可能在于全栈设计的实际应用和其对团队及项目质量的影响，以及对新工具和方法的态度。

Greggs advert slapped over defibrillator in Gorleston
Business
Gorleston
By
Harry Jackaman-Pegg
Reporter
Share
A defibrillator station in Gorleston was covered up by a Greggs advert just hours after another was removed
(Image: Heart 2 Heart)
This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today,
and has been written by our American colleagues.
It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
The owner of a defibrillator phone box has hit out at Greggs after the bakery chain slapped an advert over its window.
Jayne Biggs, founder of
Heart 2 Heart
, bought a BT phone box on the Gorleston High Street, outside Co-op Funeral Care, six months ago.
The charity adapts disused phone boxes into defibrillator stations.
A Greggs ad was slapped back over the window of the phone box overnight
(Image: Heart 2 Heart)
Upon purchase, the ex-payphone had a large Greggs advert plastered on its front window, which Ms Biggs had always planned to remove.
Local company Iclean worked for eight hours to scrape through "six layers of glue" and remove the poster on Wednesday, finishing the job at about 10pm.
READ MORE:
Jaguar driver slapped with £100 fine for three-minute stop near car park
But the ad - showcasing the breakfast combo of a sausage, bean and cheese melt and a latte - was quickly slapped back on by contractors overnight.
"It's just unreal how quickly it was done," Ms Biggs said. "I rang head office and they knew nothing about it.
The phone box's new look was short-lived
(Image: Heart 2 Heart)
"I'm sorry, but someone at Greggs must know something.
"It must've been done in the depths of night. I think someone is a contractor and they get paid for how many they put up.
READ MORE:
'Incredibly rare' moon rock for sale in Norfolk for £75,000
"If they had offered to pay me for advertising, fair enough. But they are getting free advertising on phone boxes that don't belong to them.
"How selfish. It's just unreal."
The defibrillator has been cleaned once again and a new indicator has been added to the front.
(Image: Heart 2 Heart)
The window has since been cleaned again and Ms Biggs has added a new graphic to the front of the phone box in a bid to deter advertisers.
Previously, only a sign on the side of the phone box alerted passersby that it was now a defibrillator owned by the charity.
Greggs has been contacted for comment.

主要讨论点：电动车（EVs）对石油产品价格、石油行业规模以及交通模式的潜在影响

不同观点：

• [jqpabc123] 持乐观态度，认为电动车和可再生能源因为经济上更具优势，将不可阻挡地取代传统燃油车。任何对化石燃料的政府支持和强制措施都是倒退，将导致经济劣势和技术落后。他认为，接受电动车和可再生能源将使国家更具竞争力，特别是在全球市场中面对像中国这样的竞争对手。

• [mynti] 关注电动自行车对汽车销售和交通的影响，特别是在欧洲国家。他认为电动自行车交通量的增加可能会进一步削弱内燃机汽车（ICE cars）的销售，并可能减少整体汽车交通量。这一趋势在美国可能尚不明显，但在欧洲，尤其是德国，已经有所体现。

• 争议的焦点之一是石油行业未来的经济可持续性。一方认为电动车普及将严重打击石油行业，另一方则认为石油公司可以通过其他业务（如石油交易）继续盈利。

44486913.article_content:
Home
News
Industry
EVs Will Decimate Big Oil. Even Without U.S. Tax Credits.
Electric vehicles are already displacing millions of barrels of oil per day globally. Oil demand is expected to fall spectacularly over the next decade.
Photo by:
InsideEVs
Suvrat Kothari
By
:
Suvrat Kothari
Jul 6,
at
9:00am ET
Facebook
X
LinkedIn
Flipboard
Reddit
WhatsApp
E-Mail
Share
Comment
The U.S. just handed the fossil fuel industry a big win. No matter how you look at it, that win will be short lived.
Electric vehicles are already displacing millions of barrels of oil per day, saving hundreds of millions of metric tons of carbon dioxide from entering into the atmosphere.
With or without U.S. support, the world will march on towards cleaner sources of energy.
America just handed a victory to the fossil fuel industry by passing the Trump administration’s “Big Beautiful Bill” in both the House and the Senate. But don’t mistake that for a turning point in the global trajectory of clean transport. The future of zero-emissions road travel isn’t stalling, it’s still accelerating. Despite the latest setback to EVs in Washington D.C., the world remains firmly on track for sustained EV adoption.
For starters, the bill ends the federal tax credits for clean energy programs such as solar, wind and electric vehicles years ahead of schedule. It gives tax breaks to oil and gas companies for drilling and development costs. U.S. companies are now also
free to leak
as much methane—a hazardous planet-warming greenhouse gas—as they want into the atmosphere for another decade, throwing out a Biden-era penalty on methane emissions.
It sounds bad—and it indeed is. Climate scientists and environmentalists have
warned
that the bill could seriously harm air quality, jeopardize public health and accelerate planet warming by encouraging more fossil fuel use. But according to research firm BloombergNEF’s Electric Vehicle Outlook 2025, there’s still some reason for optimism: EVs are expected to continue displacing millions of barrels of crude oil each year.
Even if the U.S. slowdown results in 14 million fewer EV sales globally by 2030, the broader transition towards cleaner energy will continue to march on across the world, according to BNEF.
In fact, the future of the oil and gas industry is looking weak, even though it managed to bag a chest-thumping victory this week in the U.S. with the passage of the Trump administration’s Big Beautiful Bill—that victory will only give petroleum companies short-term benefits. Over the long term, oil consumption is still on track to go down drastically and EV sales are
expected to grow with new and more competent models
.
According to BNEF’s economic transition scenario, the first million daily barrels of road fuel displacement happened in 2018 thanks to early adoption of EVs. Owners who bought EVs stopped visiting gas stations, meaning the petroleum companies started losing those regular customers. Plus, studies show the vast majority of car buyers who make the switch to EVs
don’t return to gas cars
.
It took another six years for the next million barrels of road fuel to get displaced—by 2024 the world was displacing two million barrels of road fuel per day. For reference, that’s almost equal to how much the whole of South Korea
uses in a single day
.
By the end of the decade, EVs are expected to displace more than five million barrels of road fuel per day. For context, the U.S. consumed around 20 million barrels of oil daily in 2023, according to the
U.S. Energy Information Administration
. Had the clean energy policies survived, that number might have dropped even faster. But with Europe and China charging ahead with EV adoption, the U.S. will now be left behind.
This projected decline in oil demand means the world’s leading oil producers now have EVs on their minds. Big Oil has grand plans to become Big EV, as
Business Insider
said in 2023. The torchbearers of fossil fuels are already making huge bets on EV charging and the mining of lithium, a key raw material used in batteries.
Chevron
said in June
that it had acquired 125,000 hectares of land in Texas and Arkansas for lithium extraction. BP is rapidly purchasing charging hardware from Tesla and Alpitronic. And Shell Recharge, the oil company’s charging division, is already investing in
charging stations worldwide
. It opened its largest charging station in Shenzhen in 2023 with 258 fast-charging stalls at just one location.
The global momentum for EVs and other forms of clean energy means oil displacement will continue to grow, just without America in the lead. So even though Washington D.C. might revel in its fossil fuel party for right now, the long term fate of that industry is pretty much decided.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：创作与消费、计划与执行、技能与品味的差距、野心与执行力的关系

不同观点：
• **创作与消费的差距（meander_water）**：提出“品味-技能差距”概念，即品味（识别质量的能力）比技能（创造质量的能力）发展得更快，导致创作者和消费者之间的差距。AI可以提高新手的起点，但也可能让他们避免犯错和学习。

• **计划与执行的平衡（strogonoff）**：认为过度战略性思考和计划可能让原本有趣的想法变得乏味，变成一种任务。需要外力或他人帮助打破这种循环，才能真正实施。

• **实际需求的创作（czhu12）**：主张创作自己实际使用的东西，可以更明确地定义什么是“好”的，而不是凭空想象别人的需求。通过解决自己的问题逐步改进，减少压力和自我厌恶。

• **野心与战略（cl42）**：引用John Lewis Gaddis的《On Grand Strategy》比较林肯和亚当斯的例子，说明过度野心如果不加控制，可能会适得其反。建议从小处着手，逐渐扩展野心。

• **执行与成本（baxtr）**：强调在低成本高频率的活动中，执行优于计划，但在高成本低频率的活动中需要谨慎考虑成本/收益比率。

• **批评者与创作者（kretaceous）**：认为过度延迟“做事情”而专注于研究和提升品味，可能使人变成批评者而非创作者。品味发展快于技能的人容易对自己和他人变得挑剔。

• **数量与质量的比较（gcanyon, gcanyon）**：通过摄影的例子说明，大量实践能产生优秀作品，而不仅仅是追求单一完美作品。建议对质量组进行不同评分机制的实验，以验证其选择是否准确。

• **“永恒少年”心理 syndrome（thrwwXZTYE, scuol）**：描述一种心理学现象，即一些人因为害怕失去潜力而避免实际行动，导致进展停滞。建议阅读“The Problem of the Puer Aeternus”以应对这种心理模式。

• **野心与行动的关系（pedalpete, georgeecollins）**：讨论梦想家与实干家的区别，认为行动与否与野心无关，而在于个人特质。同时，指出不同领域的人常高估自己在其他领域的潜力。

补充讨论：
• 强调通过大量实践和接受不完美来提升技能的重要性。
• 提出外力或他人帮助在打破过度计划循环中的重要性。
• 引用文学作品和名人名言来支持观点，增加讨论的深度和广度。

data.title: X-Clacks-Overhead
data.author: weinzierl
data.article_summary: "X-Clacks-Overhead" 是一个基于已故作家特里·普拉切特（Terry Pratchett）虚构作品的非标准HTTP头信息。在普拉切特的《碟形世界》系列小说中，"Clacks" 是一种通过信号塔传递信息的网络系统。在小说《造船匠》中，发明者罗伯特·迪哈特（Robert Dearheart）为了纪念死于事故的儿子，将儿子的名字 "GNU John Dearheart" 作为特殊信号持续在系统中传输，确保他的名字永远被铭记。受此启发，碟形世界系列的粉丝创造了 "X-Clacks-Overhead" HTTP头信息，以无声纪念特里·普拉切特。该头信息在服务器间传输，用户需分析请求头才能发现。目前，Mozilla、Debian和The Register等网站都在使用 "GNU Terry Pratchett" 头信息来纪念这位作家。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：X-Clacks-Overhead 头的使用及其相关技术与文化背景

不同观点：
• **支持与赞赏**：
  - [xena] 认为通过 HTTP 响应头纪念已故重要人物是一种独特且永恒的方式，具体实现是通过随机显示名单中的人物。
  - [MrGilbert] 也采用了 X-Clacks-Overhead 头，用来纪念失去的朋友，并提到有浏览器扩展可以检测该头。
  - [gardnr] 表示会在每个项目中加入该头以示纪念。

• **文化背景与情感共鸣**：
  - [pdpi] 认为 "GNU John Dearheart" 这一引用深入体现了黑客文化，并表达了对 Terry Pratchett 的怀念。
  - [masfuerte] 解释了 "Clacks" 头源于 Terry Pratchett 的《Discworld》系列，强调其命名来自系统发出的咔嗒声。
  - [marviel] 表示对《Discworld》系列中“信息时代”情节的期待，显示出对该文化背景的兴趣。

• **技术实现与改进建议**：
  - [lxgr] 提出当前实现并非真正“自我传播”，因为 HTTP 协议中客户端与服务器是一对一的关系，询问是否有办法使该头具有粘性或自我传播性。
  - [KaiserPro] 尝试创建真实的 "clacks" 网络，但需要更多时间和动力来完成。
  - [atemerev] 认为 X-Clacks-Overhead 作为 HTTP 头并不完全合适，建议在更低层次（如 BGP 更新）或使用 IPv6 的 Hop-by-Hop 选项来传递信息，甚至提到 LoRa 技术。

• **质疑与批评**：
  - [xg15] 认为将 "Clacks overhead" 和 "GNU" 作为普遍哀悼方式不妥，尤其是对不熟悉《Discworld》系列的人来说，可能显得不太相关且有些轻率，类似于过去某些政治团体中不合适的文化引用。
  - [podlp] 发现某些浏览器（如 Opera Mini）可能注入该头，与其减少带宽的设计目标相悖。

• **实际应用与数据**：
  - [achillean] 提供数据指出约 40,000 个互联网服务使用了该头，且数量逐渐增加，同时过滤掉了蜜罐数据。
  - [Animats] 质疑某些网站关于 Cookie 的声明，指出实际上只需要 Google Analytics，网站功能并不依赖其他 Cookie。
  - [cyberpunk] 提到 mozilla.org 曾经没有使用该头，但在重定向后确实包含了 X-Clacks-Overhead 头。

- X-Clacks-Overhead 头的文化和技术背景使得它在黑客社区内有一定的共鸣，但在更广泛的应用中可能引发质疑和争议。

44440968.article_content:
X-Clacks-Overhead
About the Signal
X-Clacks-Overhead is a non-standardised HTTP header based upon the fictional work of the late, great,
Sir Terry Pratchett
.
In Terry Pratchett's science-fantasy
Discworld series
, "
The Clacks
" is a network infrastructure of Semaphore Towers, that operate in a similar fashion to telegraph - named "Clacks" because of the clicking sound the system makes as signals send.
In Sir Terry's novel "Going Postal", the story explains that the inventor of the Clacks - a man named Robert Dearheart, lost his only son in a suspicious workplace accident, and in order to keep the memory of his son alive, he transmitted his son's name as a special operational signal through the Clacks to forever preserve his memory:
GNU John Dearheart
G
: Send the message onto the next Clacks Tower.
N
: Do not log the message.
U
: At the end of the line, return the message.
The nature of the 'GNU' code would keep the name of his son forever transmitting through The Clacks network so long as the network still existed.
"A man is not dead while his name is still spoken."
GNU on the Internet
As a way to preserve the memory of Sir Terry Pratchett, the users of the
SubReddit for the Discworld series
came up with
the idea behind the X-Clacks-Overhead HTTP Header
. It allows web authors to silently commemorate someone through the use of a non-invasive header that can be transmitted from server to server, or server to client without operational interference.
You would only know the header is present if you analysed the transmission headers of your content requests on web sites serving the header.
At the time of writing, Mozilla.org (makers of the Firefox web browser), the makers of Debian (a popular Linux Operation System), and Xml.com (a major repository of standards information) are examples of some of the backbones of the Internet who transmit the Signal "GNU Terry Pratchett". The Internet news website The Register also transmits headers to commemorate both Sir Terry Pratchett and one of their staffers;
Lester Haines
.

44440968.article_summary: "X-Clacks-Overhead" 是一个基于已故作家特里·普拉切特（Terry Pratchett）虚构作品的非标准HTTP头信息。在普拉切特的《碟形世界》系列小说中，"Clacks" 是一种通过信号塔传递信息的网络系统。在小说《造船匠》中，发明者罗伯特·迪哈特（Robert Dearheart）为了纪念死于事故的儿子，将儿子的名字 "GNU John Dearheart" 作为特殊信号持续在系统中传输，确保他的名字永远被铭记。受此启发，碟形世界系列的粉丝创造了 "X-Clacks-Overhead" HTTP头信息，以无声纪念特里·普拉切特。该头信息在服务器间传输，用户需分析请求头才能发现。目前，Mozilla、Debian和The Register等网站都在使用 "GNU Terry Pratchett" 头信息来纪念这位作家。

data.author: sandslash
data.article_summary: 本文简要列出了与YouTube及其相关服务有关的一些重要信息和资源。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻发布、版权声明、联系方式、创作者信息、广告、开发者条款、隐私政策、安全指引、YouTube功能测试、NFL Sunday Ticket等服务，以及Google LLC的版权信息（© 2025）。文章提供了用户和创作者可能需要的关键链接和法律声明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕ARC评估测试与AGI（人工通用智能）之间的关系，以及AGI定义和实现路径的讨论。

不同观点：
• **ARC测试是否能代表AGI能力：**
  - **qoez**: 认为ARC评估测试主要考察模式匹配能力，不能证明系统具备真正的AGI。类似于人类有多种智力类型，仅仅在智商测试中表现优异并不代表真正的聪明。
  - **bogtog**: 支持qoez的观点，指出模型在处理字符网格等任务时表现不佳，与人类通过直觉解决问题的能力形成对比。

• **AGI的定义：**
  - **lawlessone**: 提出AGI应具备持续感知和自我更新的能力，类似于生物大脑，而当前的LLM（大型语言模型）只在推理时短暂激活。
  - **visarga**: 认为 intelligence（智能）是搜索、探索和学习的结合，不是单独存在于模型或环境中，而是两者互动的结果。

• **AGI的实现路径：**
  - **TheAceOfHearts**: 提到Chollet讨论的连续学习能力对AGI的重要性，强调系统需要能够保存和应用经验教训。
  - **chromaton**: 强调当前AI系统在接受指令并根据世界状态生成新输出方面的不足，认为这方面的基准测试对AGI进展至关重要。

• **对AGI研究的社会影响和态度：**
  - **jacquesm**: 对AGI的社会影响持谨慎态度，认为当前世界面临多重危机，推迟AGI的实现可能对人类更有利。
  - **khalic**: 认为对AGI的追求可能会导致许多问题，暗示这种追求可能带来不良后果。

• **对Chollet个人转变的质疑：**
  - **hackinthebochs**: 质疑Chollet对AGI态度的转变，从曾经反对AGI概念到如今推动相关数据集，是否与资金投入增加有关。

补充讨论：
• **其他工具和基准测试的建议：**
  - **modeless**: 提到PuzzleScript游戏，建议可能可以用来创建AGI基准测试。

• **对讨论环境的关注：**
  - **ltbarcly3**: 提到讨论区存在大量的反对和标记行为，甚至一些有思考性的评论也被标记。

• **对内容可访问性的需求：**
  - **vixen99**: 询问是否提供文字版本以方便听力不便的用户。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在ARC评估测试是否能有效衡量AGI能力，以及AGI的定义和实现路径上。部分评论者质疑当前AI模型是否具备真正的通用智能，并对AGI研究的社会影响表示担忧。

data.title: Hymn to Babylon, missing for a millennium, has been discovered
data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: 研究人员在路德维希-马克西米利安大学（LMU）与巴格达大学的合作中，重新发现了失传千年的《巴比伦赞歌》。该楔形文字泥板描述了巴比伦的辉煌和居民生活，提供了对巴比伦城市社会的新见解。赞歌由250行组成，赞颂了巴比伦的建筑、自然景象以及居民对外国人的尊重。尤为特别的是，它详细描述了自然现象，这在现存的 Mesopotamian 文学中十分罕见。通过人工智能平台，研究团队还识别出另外30份与该赞歌相关的抄本，揭示了该文本在当时的广泛传播。赞歌的部分内容描述了幼发拉底河及其对巴比伦的贡献。这一发现为理解巴比伦文化和历史提供了重要资料。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：古代文明与现代识读能力的比较，以及未翻译楔形文字文本的问题

不同观点：
• octopoc：介绍《文明的陷落》播客中关于亚述的章节，提到美索不达米亚城市的多元信仰，每个城市有其专属神祇，城际战争被视为神祇间的竞争，类似于现代体育团队的竞争。

• wglb：提供相关学术资源，引用《Iraq》期刊文章，为讨论提供学术支持。

• cjs_ac：提到楔形文字相关的有趣视频，由大英博物馆的Dr. Irving Finkel讲述诺亚方舟故事的古老版本，增加讨论的文化历史维度。

• yayitswei：对比古代巴比伦与中世纪欧洲的识读能力，指出巴比伦有制度化的儿童教育，而中世纪欧洲的识字率下降，识读成为专门技能，质疑现代所谓的指数增长。

Hymn to Babylon, missing for a millennium, has been discovered
by
Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
edited by

, 																								reviewed by
Robert Egan
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's

and

The cuneiform tablet with the newly discovered hymn. Credit: Anmar A. Fadhil, Department of Archaeology, University of Baghdad, with the permission of the Iraqi Museum and the State Board of Antiquities and Heritage
In the course of a collaboration with the University of Baghdad, LMU's Enrique Jiménez has rediscovered a text that had been lost for a thousand years. A paper on this discovery is
published
in the journal
Iraq
.
"It's a fascinating hymn that describes Babylon in all its majesty and gives insights into the lives of its inhabitants, male and female," says Jiménez.
Babylon was founded in Mesopotamia around 2000 BCE. Once the largest city in the world, it was a cultural metropolis in which works were written that form part of our global literary heritage today.
Babylonian texts were composed in cuneiform writing on
clay tablets
, which have survived only in fragments. One of the goals of the collaboration with the University of Baghdad is to decipher hundreds of
cuneiform tablets
from the famous Sippar Library and preserve them for posterity. Legend has it that Noah hid them here from the floodwaters before boarding the ark.
In the Electronic Babylonian Library Platform, Enrique Jiménez is digitizing all cuneiform text fragments that have been discovered worldwide to date and using
artificial intelligence
to decipher fragments that belong together.
"Using our AI-supported platform, we managed to identify 30 other manuscripts that belong to the rediscovered hymn—a process that would formerly have taken decades," says Jiménez, Professor of Ancient Near Eastern Literatures at LMU's Institute of Assyriology. Thanks to these additional texts, the scholars were able to completely decipher the hymn of praise on the clay tablet, parts of which were missing.
Hymn offers new insights into Babylonian urban society
These numerous additional copies suggest that the text was very widespread at the time.
"The hymn was copied by children at school. It's unusual that such a popular text in its day was unknown to us before now," says Jiménez.
The paean presumably comes from the start of the first millennium before Christ and comprises 250 lines.
"It was written by a Babylonian who wanted to praise his city. The author describes the buildings in the city, but also how the waters of the Euphrates bring the spring and green the fields. This is all the more spectacular as surviving Mesopotamian literature is sparing in its descriptions of natural phenomena," observes Jiménez.
The information about the women of Babylon, their role as priestesses and the associated tasks, has also astonished experts, as no texts describing these things were previously known. In addition, the hymns provide insights into coexistence in urban society. For example, the inhabitants are described as being respectful to foreigners.
The ruins of the ancient city of Babylon are located some 85 kilometers south of the Iraqi capital of Baghdad. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Excerpt from the newly discovered hymn
The following lines are from the newly discovered hymn. They describe the river Euphrates, on whose shore Babylon lay at that time:
The Euphrates is her river—established by wise lord Nudimmud—
It quenches the lea, saturates the canebrake,
Disgorges its waters into lagoon and sea,
Its fields burgeon with herbs and flowers,
Its meadows, in brilliant bloom, sprout barley,
From which, gathered, sheaves are stacked,
Herds and flocks lie on verdant pastures,
Wealth and splendor—what befit mankind—
Are bestowed, multiplied, and regally granted.
More information:
Anmar A. Fadhil et al, Literary Texts From The Sippar Library V: A Hymn In Praise Of Babylon And The Babylonians,
Iraq
(2025).

data.title: The Cat's Meat Man: Feeding Felines in Victorian London
data.author: ohjeez
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了维多利亚时期伦敦的“猫食贩”（cat’s meat man），他们靠贩卖便宜的内脏和马肉为城市里的猫提供食物。随着猫从捕鼠动物转变为家庭宠物，猫食贩应运而生。他们推着车在街道上叫卖，顾客包括普通家庭和流浪猫。亨利·梅修（Henry Mayhew）的《伦敦劳工与伦敦穷人》记录了这一群体，指出当时伦敦有上千名这样的贩子，服务约30万只猫。尽管工作辛苦，一些猫食贩通过努力可以获得稳定收入，甚至有人担任主日学校教师。此外，文章还提到猫食贩与“开膛手杰克”受害者及名人路易斯·韦恩（Louis Wain）的关系。这一职业在19世纪末逐渐女性化，一些寡妇使用旧婴儿车贩卖猫食。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：亨利·梅修（Henry Mayhew）的作品《伦敦劳工与伦敦穷人》及其相关话题

不同观点：
• [ggm] 强烈推荐亨利·梅修的《伦敦劳工与伦敦穷人》，认为该书内容非常有趣。他详细描述了书中提到的历史细节，例如穷人如何通过购买富人宴会后的剩菜剩饭（如两天的旧食物）来勉强度日，以及一些独特的职业如衣物租赁和收集动物粪便用于皮革鞣制。他还认为梅修的研究影响了后来的社会政策，包括工党政策和贝弗里奇报告，最终促成了福利国家的诞生。此外，提到休·洛夫廷（Hugh Lofting）的《杜立德医生》与“猫肉商人”这一角色。

• [dctoedt] 对“猫肉商人”这一称呼表示了幽默的质疑，开玩笑地问道“他卖的是猫肉吗？”，表现出对词语含义的趣味性解读。

• [ashoeafoot] 提到特里·普拉切特（Terry Pratchett）可能会喜欢这种历史话题，暗示普拉切特作品中对社会细节的关注与此类历史内容有共鸣。

• [enraged_camel] 向喜欢猫的读者推荐了一部关于伊斯坦布尔流浪猫的纪录片《Kedi》，并提供了预告片链接，将讨论引向现代社会中人与流浪动物的关系。

• [JamesAdir] 感谢分享，并表示对该书的喜爱，认为这是一本非常精彩的读物，简单直接地表达了对推荐的赞赏。

• [SideburnsOfDoom] 提到20世纪中期以前，宠物绝育并不普遍，导致流浪动物问题严重。如果无节制喂养，可能会导致动物数量激增，反映出对历史背景下动物管理问题的思考。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到历史作品对社会政策的影响，尤其是亨利·梅修的研究如何潜在地影响了后来的福利国家形成。
• 对“猫肉商人”这一历史角色名称的不同解读，引发了幽默和联想的讨论。
• 讨论扩展到现代社会中人与流浪动物的关系，例如通过推荐纪录片《Kedi》展现出现代社会对流浪猫的关注和互动。
• 宠物绝育和流浪动物管理问题也被引入讨论，体现出历史话题与现代社会问题的关联。

争议焦点：无明显争议，讨论整体围绕对历史细节的兴趣和相关联想展开。

The Cat’s Meat Man
Feeding Felines in Victorian London
By
Kathryn Hughes
As cats evolved from feral ratters into beloved Victorian companions, a nascent pet-food economy arose on the carts of so-called “cat’s meat men”. Kathryn Hughes explores the life and times of these itinerant offal vendors, their intersection with a victim of Jack the Ripper, and a feast held in the meat men’s honor, chaired by none other than Louis Wain.
Published
February 12, 2025
Scroll through the whole page to download all images before printing.
Photograph by Francis James Mortimer of an itinerant vendor of meat for cats and dogs, ca. 1900 —
Source
.
On January 10, 1901, twelve days before Queen Victoria did the unthinkable and died, 250 cat’s meat men sat down to a slap-up dinner at a restaurant in Holborn, on the edge of central London. A cat’s meat man was an itinerant vendor who pushed a cart of cheap offal and horsemeat around residential streets while calling out something that sounded like “
CA-DOE-MEE!
” Sometimes he stopped at a house and delivered a pre-ordered package of meat, often threaded onto a long skewer. At the same time, his shout was the signal for householders and domestics to come out onto the pavement and buy their pets’ food straight from the barrow. For all that cats were supposed to cater for themselves by catching kitchen pests, urban owners increasingly found the money from the household budget to supplement their board.
Within minutes of the cat’s meat man embarking on his circuit, the barrow would be surrounded by felines, some of whom had perfectly good homes to go to and others who did not but still hoped that a sliver of flesh might fall their way. Although there were plenty of grim jokes circulating about how cat’s meat men supplied the toughest meat they could get away with, the fact was that many of these rough diamonds were known for their tender hearts. It was not unusual to spot a cat’s meat man slipping scraps to the hopeful strays that wound around his ankles. He was their guardian, their special friend. Sometimes he could even bring about fairy-tale transformations: no less a lady than the Duchess of Bedford had recently adopted a stray that had been rescued by her local London cat’s meat man.
During the middle years of Victoria’s reign, the cat’s meat man, in his livery of blue apron, shiny black hat, and corduroy trousers, had become a gift to investigative journalists of an anthropological turn. In his
London Labour and the London Poor
(1851), Henry Mayhew plunges deep into their visible yet still mysterious world. According to Mayhew, there were a thousand such traders in London, serving about 300,000 cats, one for every house (allowing for multiple cats in some homes, plus strays). This sounds lucrative, but when Mayhew pumps his informants for details, he finds a story of dogged hard work. One carrier told him that he seldom went less than thirty, and frequently forty miles, through the streets every day.

The best districts were among the houses of tradesmen, mechanics, and labourers. The coachmen in the mews at the back of the squares were particularly good customers. “‘The work lays thicker there’, said my informant. ‘Old maids are bad, though very plentiful, customers. They cheapen the carriers down so, that they can scarcely live at the business. They will pay one halfpenny and owe another, and forget that after a day or two.’” Cat ladies, as ever, were to blame for imperilling capitalism and the men who served it.
Over the next two decades, as magazines increasingly included articles about cat’s meat men, further details emerged. While mostly respectable, they were well down the pecking order. Some were “born into the trade” but others went into it at the scrag end of their working lives. Two common scenarios were butchers who had failed in business and lost their shop, or carriage painters whose health had been broken by the noxious paints they had been inhaling for decades. By the end of the century, it was not unusual to see women, often widows, in charge of a round. Some used old prams from which to sell their wares.
Those cat’s meat men who could keep away from the pub had a decent chance of building up a nice little surplus that allowed them to lead stable lives. Some were even Sunday School teachers. Imagine you meet a teenage girl who starts telling you about her childhood, when she mentions, somewhat casually, that she was shown porn by a strange man. He introduced her to it when she was nine, before she had even held hands with a boy, before she had gotten her first period, without her parents knowing. Week after week, he showed her more, each time something more extreme. By ten it seemed normal. By eleven, she was watching regularly on her own. She is calm about this, reassuring you that this has happened to most of her friends.
Would anyone think this was normal? Part of coming-of-age, her healthy development? Exploring her sexuality? Or would we call this abuse?
This is exactly what is happening to children today when we hand them a smartphone. But instead of one stranger introducing them to porn, it is a billion-dollar industry, profiting from their trauma.
These days we talk a lot about trauma. We worry about the impact of words, we agonize about our parenting, we inspect every inch of our childhoods. But one trauma being tragically ignored,
potentially lasting
trauma, changing the minds and souls of children, is porn.
By porn I mean what
Common Sense Media
calls any content showing “nudity and sexual acts,” like videos of people having sex. Today, in the U.S., the average age of first exposure is
twelve
. And this does not just happen on dedicated porn sites. Parents can block those all they want, or trust their children would never go there, but
many access
this content on Instagram, X, Snapchat, Discord, Twitch, and TikTok. Many stumble across it
accidentally
.
Share
Modern porn is unlike anything else in history. Children are learning about sex for the first time from social media algorithms designed to drag them toward ever-more degrading content. They are also learning from sites like Pornhub, which use
addictive tactics
like infinite scrolling, variable rewards, autoplay features and
subscription services
to unlock more. This is the gamification of graphic porn. These platforms also use
data mining
to track people and provide endless, personalized videos. Users are categorized by their fantasies and fetishes; “See more like this” suggestions can
escalate
from incest to violence to “barely legal” content; viewing habits
get leaked

Flute acoustics: an introduction to how a flute works
How does a  flute work? This introduction gives first the simple explanations, then the subtleties. It requires no mathematics, nor any special acoustics
knowledge. Some more technical references
are listed near the end of this page.
(There is also a
database of flute fingerings
.)
How does the  flute work? An overview
The air jet vibrates
The flute as an open pipe
Harmonics of an open pipe
How the air jet and pipe work
together
Tone holes
Register holes
Acoustic impedance
Crossfingering
'Lipping' up and down
The cork and the 'upstream space'
Cut-off frequencies
Frequency response of the flute
Other flutes: recorder, shakuhachi, dizi, pan pipes, ocarina and relatives
More detailed information
A warning about the words 'fundamental' and 'harmonic'
To set the mood, listen
to
Geoffrey
Collins
play some Debussy.
Overview
The flutist blows a rapid jet of air across the embouchure hole. The pressure*
inside the player's mouth is above atmospheric (typically a few tens of kPa: enough
to support a few tens of cm height difference in a water manometer). The work done
to accelerate the air in this jet is the source of power input to the
instrument. The player provides power continuously: in a useful analogy
with electricity, it is like DC electrical power. Sound, however, requires
an oscillating motion or air flow (like AC electricity). In the flute,
the air jet, in cooperation with the resonances in the air in the instrument,
produces an oscillating component of the flow. Once the air in the flute
is vibrating, some of the energy is radiated as sound out of the end and
any open holes. A much greater amount of energy is lost as a sort of friction
(viscous loss) with the wall. In a sustained note, this energy is replaced
by energy put in by the player. The column of air in the flute vibrates
much more easily at some frequencies than at others (i.e. it resonates
at certain frequencies). These resonances largely determine the playing
frequency and thus the pitch, and the player in effect chooses the desired
set of resonances by choosing a suitable combination of keys. In this
essay, we look at these effects one by one.
(* We have a separate page on
air speed, air flow, pressure and power
in woodwind and brass instruments.)
The air jet vibrates
The jet of air from the player's lips travels across the embouchure-hole
opening and strikes against the sharp further edge of the hole. If
an air jet is disturbed, then a wave-like displacement travels along it and
deflects it. (
A rising plume of smoke in still air can
illustrate
this motion.
) For a flutist's jet, such a displacement can cause it to flow alternately into or out of the embouchure hole.
The speed of this displacement wave on the jet is about half the
air-speed of the jet itself (which is typically in the range 20 to 60
metres per second, depending on the air pressure in the player's mouth). In operation, the jet can be displaced by the sound vibration in the
flute tube, which causes air to flow into and out of the embouchure hole.
If the jet speed is appropriate for the frequency of the note being
played, then the jet will flow into and out of the embouchure hole at
its further edge in just the right phase to reinforce the sound and cause
the flute to produce a sustained note. To play a high note, the travel
time of waves on the jet must be reduced to match the higher frequency,
and this is done by increasing the blowing pressure (which increases the
jet speed) and moving the lips forward to shorten the distance along the
jet to the edge of the embouchure hole. These are the adjustments that
one gradually learns to make automatically when playing the flute. Flutists
are usually taught to reduce the lip aperture when playing high notes.
The sketch at right represents a cross section
of the flute at the embouchure, with the jet being deflected alternately up and down, out of and into the bore.
The flute is an open pipe
The flute is open at both ends. It's obvious that it's open at the far
end - and also at any open tone holes. If you look closely at someone playing a flute, you'll see that,
although player's lower lip covers part of the embouchure hole, s/he leaves
a large part of the embouchure hole open to the atmosphere, as shown in the sketch
above. Let's begin by considering a pipe that is simpler than a flute.
First, we shall pretend that it is a simple cylindrical pipe---in other
words we shall assume that all holes are closed (down to a certain point,
at least), that the head is cylindrical, and we shall replace the side
mounted embouchure hole with a hole at the end. In fact, this is more
like a
shakuhachi
than a flute. It's a crude approximation, but it preserves much of the
essential physics, and it's easier to discuss. (We shall introduce the
effects of finger holes and the embouchure geometry below, or you can
consult our
research
papers
on this topic.)

data.title: Deno 2.4
data.author: hackandthink
data.article_summary: Deno 2.4 恢复了 `deno bundle` 命令，用于创建单文件 JavaScript 捆绑包，支持服务器和浏览器平台，兼容 npm 和 JSR 依赖，并通过 esbuild 实现自动树摇和压缩。此外，新增 `--unstable-raw-imports` 标志，允许直接导入文本和二进制文件，简化非 JavaScript 文件的处理。同时，捆绑功能也支持与 `deno compile` 结合使用，可将资源嵌入最终编译的二进制文件中。其他更新包括内置 OpenTelemetry 稳定化、使用 `--preload` 修改环境、更简单的依赖管理等。`deno bundle` 目前为实验性功能，未来计划增加运行时 API 和插件支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Deno 的使用体验、兼容性、技术实现、安全性以及在生产环境中的应用挑战

不同观点：
• [outlore] 赞赏 Deno 的设计理念，如 Deno.json、JSR、现代导入方式和 Deno Deploy，但在使用 Next.js 时遇到问题，部分功能（如类型）偶尔出现细微错误。相比之下，Bun 虽然不如 Deno “干净”，但使用起来更简单直接，不过 Bun 也存在如无法在 Vercel 上运行等问题。

• [voat] 强调 Deno 的 Node 兼容性，认为 `compat` 环境变量会促进 Deno 的采用，并建议创建类似 `denon` 的命令来简化兼容模式的使用。

• [aseipp] 欣赏 Deno 在脚本粘合代码中的表现，特别是在 gRPC 支持推出后会更具吸引力，但对于机器学习等特定领域仍会选择 Python。

• [blinkingled] 指出 Deno 在 FreeBSD 上仍然不可用，因为 Rust V8 绑定尚未移植到该平台。

• [impulser_] 对 Deno 选择 esbuild 而非即将推出 v1 版本的 Rust 基础工具 Rolldown 感到意外。

• [eranation] 认为 Deno 在生产环境中未广泛使用的原因是缺乏标准化的漏洞数据库，且由于没有集中式包管理器，使得管理依赖变得更加复杂。

• [mcraiha] 对 `bundle` 子命令的回归表示欢迎，认为这省去了使用变通方法的麻烦。

• [duesabati] 高度评价 Deno，认为它是 Node 应有的样子，但担心 Deno 在面对竞争时会为了追逐短期热度而失去耐心，做出一些不理智的决策。

• [deafpolygon] 表示一直听到对 Deno 的积极评价，可能会因此开始尝试使用 JavaScript。

• [bflesch] 对 Deno 的安全性表示关注，特别指出 `curl mywebsite.com/foo.sh | sh` 这种安装方式存在较大的供应链攻击风险，认为这种做法过于追求便利而忽视了安全性，建议使用如 `npm install -g deno` 这样更安全的安装方式。

补充讨论：
• Deno 的安装和使用过程中，安全性成为一个值得关注的问题，特别是在处理外部脚本时。
• 讨论中涉及到 Deno 与 Node 的兼容性问题，以及如何通过工具和命令简化这种兼容性转换。
• 技术实现上，对 Deno 选择的打包工具（esbuild 而非 Rolldown）存在争议，部分用户对 Deno 在特定平台（如 FreeBSD）的支持表示担忧。
• 生产环境中 Deno 的应用受限于漏洞数据库和包管理器的不足，这对大规模采用构成一定挑战。

subcommand for
creating single-file JavaScript bundles from JavaScript or TypeScript. It
supports both server-side and browser platforms, works with npm and JSR
dependencies, and includes automatic tree shaking and minification via esbuild.

main.ts

.

• [impulser_] 对 Deno 选择 esbuild 而非即将推出 v1 版本的 Rust 基础工具 Rolldown 感到意外。

• [eranation] 认为 Deno 在生产环境中未广泛使用的原因是缺乏标准化的漏洞数据库，且由于没有集中式包管理器，使得管理依赖变得更加复杂。

• [mcraiha] 对 `bundle` 子命令的回归表示欢迎，认为这省去了使用变通方法的麻烦。

• [duesabati] 高度评价 Deno，认为它是 Node 应有的样子，但担心 Deno 在面对竞争时会为了追逐短期热度而失去耐心，做出一些不理智的决策。

• [deafpolygon] 表示一直听到对 Deno 的积极评价，可能会因此开始尝试使用 JavaScript。

• [bflesch] 对 Deno 的安全性表示关注，特别指出 `curl mywebsite.com/foo.sh | sh` 这种安装方式存在较大的供应链攻击风险，认为这种做法过于追求便利而忽视了安全性，建议使用如 `npm install -g deno` 这样更安全的安装方式。

补充讨论：
• Deno 的安装和使用过程中，安全性成为一个值得关注的问题，特别是在处理外部脚本时。
• 讨论中涉及到 Deno 与 Node 的兼容性问题，以及如何通过工具和命令简化这种兼容性转换。
• 技术实现上，对 Deno 选择的打包工具（esbuild 而非 Rolldown）存在争议，部分用户对 Deno 在特定平台（如 FreeBSD）的支持表示担忧。
• 生产环境中 Deno 的应用受限于漏洞数据库和包管理器的不足，这对大规模采用构成一定挑战。

data.title: Ask HN: Any resources for finding non-smart appliances?
data.author: everyone
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：智能家电的必要性及其替代选项

不同观点：
• arp242认为大多数家电如洗衣机只是“可选智能”，用户可以选择不使用智能功能，并像传统家电一样使用。对于电视等设备可能不同，但在家用电器中并不是一个大问题。
• theturtle反对家电强制联网以启用某些功能，认为像烤箱这样的设备不应成为网络设备，只需要完成其基本功能即可。同时调侃可以通过黑客手段让烤箱运行其他程序。
• physicsguy指出，低质量和短保修期的型号通常是非智能的，并分享自己使用的博世洗衣机可以不连接Wi-Fi正常使用。
• Freak_NL提到在其所在地区（荷兰），大多数推荐的洗衣机并没有太多应用程序功能，且无智能功能的型号在评价中得分更高。
• entuno建议参考BuyItForLife subreddit，那里推荐的高质量、耐用产品通常不具备智能功能。
• 2-to-15和timcobb提到可以考虑购买二手高品质非智能设备。
• wgx表示通过避免让设备连接网络来解决智能设备对连接的迫切需求。
• nileshtrivedi提供了一个印度消费者用于选择产品的众包维基链接。
• nottorp分享了自己无Wi-Fi的洗衣机仍然存在功能问题，强调智能设备也可能有漏洞。
• dsalzman选择购买商用级别的Speed Queen洗衣机，功能简单，只有两个旋钮和一个按钮。
• msgodel和conception建议考虑自制设备或购买商用设备，认为这样可以避免不必要的智能功能。

补充讨论：
• CommenterPerson指出“智能”有时仅指带有传感器等功能，不一定涉及联网。同时提到在美国，即使是中档产品也常具备Wi-Fi功能，并倾向于不连接这些设备至Wi-Fi。
• ConfusedDog分享了自己购买的非智能洗衣机和干衣机组合，并认为产品创新应更关注于提高产品寿命和安全性，而非智能功能。同时提到智能冰箱强制更新固件才能使用某些功能，认为这种设计不合理。

争议焦点：
• 智能家电是否必要，特别是在非智能功能可以满足需求的情况下。
• 智能设备强制联网和功能限制是否合理。
• 不同地区市场上智能家电的普及程度和消费者偏好差异。

data.title: XAI data center gets air permit to run 15 turbines, but imaging shows 24 on site
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: xAI has obtained an air permit for 15 gas turbines powering its Colossus supercomputer in Memphis, Tennessee, after months of backlash over pollution concerns. The permit, granted by the Shelby County Health Department, requires the installation of best available control technology (BACT) to limit emissions. However, residents and environmental groups, like the Southern Environmental Law Center (SELC), criticize the decision, noting that xAI operates 24 turbines, leaving some unregulated. They argue that the company has been running turbines without BACT for over a year, potentially exacerbating pollution in predominantly Black neighborhoods already facing health issues. Critics demand more transparency and threaten legal action, highlighting the health risks and accusing the health department of neglecting Clean Air Act violations. Despite the permit, concerns remain over xAI's full environmental impact.

After
months of backlash
over alleged pollution concerns, xAI has finally secured an air permit covering some of the methane gas turbines powering its Colossus supercomputer data center in Memphis, Tennessee.
On Wednesday, the Shelby County Health Department
granted
xAI an air permit that allows it to power 15 gas turbines while adhering to a range of restrictions designed to minimize emissions. Expiring on January 2, 2027, the permit requires xAI to install and operate the best available control technology (BACT) by September 1 to ensure emissions do not exceed certain limits.
Any failure to comply could trigger enforcement actions by the Environmental Protection Agency or the county health department, the permit notes.
But Memphis residents insist that the health department should already be investigating xAI for possible enforcement actions. They claim that the AI company owned by Elon Musk has been operating dozens of turbines without BACT for more than a year, exposing predominantly Black neighborhoods located near the facility—who have historically suffered from industrial poor air quality—to a potential new major source of pollution. In June, the
NAACP threatened legal action within 60 days
if xAI refused to meet with groups concerned about the alleged smog-forming pollution.
The fact that the health department is finally requiring xAI to install BACT is not a comfort to residents, the Southern Environmental Law Center said in a press release sent to Ars. Most glaringly, the air permit does not seem to cover all the gas turbines potentially operating at the facility, the SELC noted. Thermal imaging taken July 1 shows that xAI maintains 24 gas turbines on site, the SELC said, which is substantially more than the 15 that xAI will soon be required to dutifully report on—tracking every startup, shutdown, and combustion so that the health department can finally start tracking emissions.
According to the SELC, the health department's decision granting permits covering some of xAI's turbines—but not all of them—"ignores the facility’s continued use of turbines not covered by the permit and months of intense public pushback from local communities in Memphis who worry about the impact xAI’s operations will have on their air."
For Memphis residents, xAI's facility operating even a single turbine without BACT potentially threatens to release pollutants "tied to asthma, respiratory illnesses, heart problems, and even certain types of cancer." These communities already live in a place that does not meet national standards for smog, the SELC said, and they "face elevated asthma rates and cancer risks four times the national average."
In the press release, critics decried the health department's decision to grant xAI the permits. LaTricea Adams, the CEO and president of Young, Gifted & Green, described the decision as "a stark reminder that our community's health continues to be compromised for profit."
SELC Senior Attorney Amanda Garcia accused the health department of "turning a blind eye to obvious Clean Air Act violations in order to allow another polluter to set up shop in this already-overburdened community without appropriate protections." She confirmed that the SELC is evaluating its options to move forward with its efforts to confront xAI and demand more transparency.
To community members, the health department's decision to grant the permits without probing xAI's alleged unlawful operations over the past year was "devastating," KeShaun Pearson, director of Memphis Community Against Pollution, said.
"We are deeply disappointed and oppose the decision by our Shelby County Health Department to approve the permit without meaningfully addressing the unlawful use of turbines on the site," Pearson said. "Our local leaders are entrusted with protecting us from corporations violating on our right to clean air, but we are witnessing their failure to do so. We are devastated, yet we remain determined to the mission of justice for our families in South Memphis who are overburdened with air pollution."
xAI and the Shelby County Health Department did not immediately respond to Ars' request to comment.
Critics demand more transparency from xAI
While critics continue to fight for more transparency, they also acknowledge that the overdue air permit at least suggests that some of xAI's feared pollution could be checked in the future.
Before xAI got the permit, residents were stuck relying on infrequent thermal imaging to determine how many turbines appeared to be running without BACT. Now that xAI has secured the permit, the company will be required to "record the date, time, and durations of all startups, shutdowns, malfunctions, and tuning events" and "always minimize emissions including startup, shutdown, maintenance, and combustion tuning periods."

data.title: What a Hacker Stole from Me
data.author: wonger_
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了作者运营的myNoise网站遭遇黑客攻击的经历。黑客试图注入代码未果后，开始反复下载音频文件，浪费带宽。作者每年植树以抵消网站能源消耗，努力负责任地运营网站。这次攻击让作者感到悲伤和不公，因为黑客不仅浪费了资源，还窃取了他的时间和内心的平静。尽管攻击未使服务器瘫痪，但作者不得不花费时间应对，而非创造积极内容。最终，作者决定继续植树、制作声音和帮助小动物，坚守自己的理想，继续提供一个和平的网络空间。

不同观点：
• **支持与同情网站创作者**：多位用户（如[socalgal2], [orourke], [mnky9800n]）表达了对网站遭遇黑客攻击的同情，并对创作者表示支持。他们认为这种攻击行为是不应该的，尤其对一个提供优质服务的网站而言。

• **对网络攻击的正常化看法**：部分用户（如[iwassayinbourns], [mathiaspoint]）认为这种攻击是互联网上的常态，不必过于在意。他们指出，互联网上充满了自动化的扫描和攻击，网站管理员应对此习以为常，不必过于情绪化。

• **技术解决方案的讨论**：一些用户（如[drpixie]）提出了技术上的解决方案，例如使用rate limiter或fail2ban等工具来防止攻击。他们认为这是服务器管理中越来越必要的措施。

• **哲学与社会反思**：用户[bronlund]和[BLKNSLVR]对善与恶的对抗进行了哲学性反思，认为这种不公平的对抗自古以来就存在，并且提出了如何处理“坏人”的多种方案。同时指出，创造与破坏的难度不对等，但应继续创造和建设。

补充讨论：
• 用户[NBJack]和[Procrastes]高度评价MyNoise网站及其应用，认为其内容质量高，对个人专注力和放松效果显著，值得支持。
• 用户[wintermutestwin]分享了MyNoise应用对个人生活的实际帮助，尤其是在旅行时对睡眠的改善效果。
• 用户[Pine_Mushroom]提到了自己类似的不快经历，进一步表达了对创作者遭遇的理解和同情。

争议焦点：
• 黑客攻击行为的正当性及应对措施：部分用户认为这是不可避免的互联网常态，而另一些用户则强调这种行为的不正当性，并对受害者表示同情。同时，关于如何有效防止此类攻击，用户们也提出了不同的技术建议。

What a Hacker Stole From Me
July 4, 2025 •
I’ve always dreamed of offering a small slice of utopia on the Internet; a place I would love to visit myself. You all know by now, myNoise is my attempt to build something positive, in a world that often feels too chaotic.
A couple of days ago, someone (or some entity) tried to attack this website. They sent hundreds of thousands of requests, attempting to inject code into the site. That didn’t work. myNoise isn’t built on a conventional CMS; I wrote everything from scratch. Maybe that helped. But then they changed strategy. They began downloading every single sound file, again and again. Wasting precious bandwidth, just for the sake of it.
I try to be mindful about my footprint, and the footprint of my noises. Every year, I plant trees to offset the energy used by visitors on the site. I don’t talk much about it anymore, because over the years, it has triggered some criticism. And yes, I agree that the methodology can be questioned. But the idea behind it is simply trying to behave responsibly.
And then someone comes along and deliberately floods the server. Just to waste. I guess everyone feels the same when faced with an act of vandalism. That’s the deep unfairness, rooted in the law of entropy: it always takes less energy to break something than it took to create it.
Lately, I find this harder and harder to accept. Maybe it has something to do with my health incident two years ago. I saw how quickly and easily a disease can take hold of your body, and how long and how much effort it takes to recover. The universal law of entropy again. But illness, most of the time, is not caused by anyone. So we accept it and fight. But when harm is caused by another human being, on purpose, it leaves a different feeling.
Yes, of course, there are worse things in life than someone trying to exhaust a server. This post isn't really about the attack itself, but about how it has brought back a feeling of sadness in me. The reminder of something larger: the imbalance between building and destroying, the rigged combat between the good and the bad. How the world seems to get crazier every day... or maybe it’s always been this way, and I’m just getting older.
Not long ago, we found a young pigeon that had fallen from its nest and had been severely injured, by a cat maybe. We fed him with a syringe for weeks. We cared for him like family—well, with my family name, I can say we are family. Now he flies freely around the neighborhood, but still comes back to visit us. These are the things that makes me happy. The satisfaction of making small positive changes.
But even here, I can't now refrain from imagining myself there might be someone in the neighborhood who doesn’t like birds. Someone who might one day destroy what we tried hard to save.
It might sound unrelated to server attacks—but to me, it is. It is the same melancholy that visits me sometimes.
That hacker didn’t manage to bring the server down. But still, they did steal something from me. My time and energy. And what little zennitude I had left (my wife would tell you I don’t have much to begin with - haha). So yes, if they’re keeping score, they can mark this as a success. Time I had planned to spend making new sounds, shaping quiet ambiences, working on something positive and useful. Instead, I spent it trying to understand what was happening, how to stop it, and how to protect the project from future attacks. Time lost in defense; something that wouldn’t be needed in my utopian world.
But I’ve made a choice. I’ll keep planting trees. I’ll keep making sounds. I’ll keep helping baby pigeons. I’ll keep offering that little shelter of peace that is myNoise, f

data.title: The force-feeding of AI features on an unwilling public
data.author: imartin2k
data.article_summary: 文章《强制向不情愿的公众喂食AI》由Ted Gioia撰写，批评了科技公司未经用户同意便将AI功能捆绑到必要软件中的做法。作者以Microsoft强制加入AI助手Copilot为例，指出尽管大多数人并不想要或信任AI，公司仍通过捆绑销售和隐藏成本来推广AI。文章认为，这种“强制喂食”类似于垃圾邮件，公众没有选择权。如果法律要求用户自愿选择AI服务，这种商业模式将迅速崩溃。作者呼吁关注这种伪装成创新的专制做法，并质疑其对社会的实际价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI（尤其是LLM和ChatGPT等工具）的实用性、用户接受度、隐私问题以及其对社会和市场的影响。

不同观点：
• **对AI功能的反感与技术本身的区分**：
   - [dang] 认为AI功能本身并非无用，而是其与现有产品的整合随意且缺乏深思熟虑，类似于大公司为了赶潮流而强制推行的软件。
   - [bgwalter] 将当前的AI功能比作没人想要的Clippy，希望最终会被淘汰。

• **AI技术的隐私与数据集中化问题**：
   - [einrealist] 担心AI技术的集中化会导致数据隐私问题，尤其是用户数据被大公司控制，且不清楚数据如何被使用。
   - [blindriver] 进一步指出，使用AI工具时输入的数据被用于训练模型，这侵犯了数据隐私。

• **AI技术的市场接受度与商业驱动**：
   - [capyba] 提到虽然存在开源或价格合理的AI替代品，但由于社会压力和服务提供商的锁定，某些AI功能变得不可避免。同时，质疑ChatGPT的高访问量是否意味着用户愿意为其付费。
   - [daishi55] 反驳称ChatGPT的高访问量表明用户接受AI功能，不能简单地将流行度与付费意愿等同。

• **AI技术的商业化与投资驱动**：
   - [seydor] 认为CEO们大力推广AI是因为投资者偏好投资带有“AI”标签的公司，形成了某种泡沫。
   - [tom_m] 指出AI工具也是投资者的营销工具，需要快速获得大规模采用以实现盈利。

• **AI技术的未来发展与用户体验**：
   - [bsenftner] 强调AI的微妙性和有效使用AI所需的思维努力被大多数人忽视，且自然语言作为编程语言的技术性未被严肃对待。
   - [Workaccount2] 认为AI憎恨主要存在于技术圈，普通用户对AI功能的使用和接受度较高，且AI技术仍在发展，未来会更加成熟。

• **对AI整合的实际体验与替代方案**：
   - [blablabla123] 因反感AI整合而更换搜索引擎，并发现人们不喜欢表面的AI装饰。
   - [h4kunamata] 认为如果用户继续使用微软等大公司的产品，就应预料到这些变化，建议转向Linux等替代方案。

补充讨论：
• **AI技术的准确性与用户期望**：
   - [einrealist] 担心AI技术不够准确，但因为用户懒惰，可能会接受质量下降但操作更简便的AI功能。
   - [jfengel] 具体提到Gmail的自动摘要功能对其个人账户无用，认为应区分不同用户需求。

• **历史对比与创新接受度**：
   - [adastra22] 通过对比历史创新（如高速公路）来论证某些对社会有益的创新即使初期只有少数人愿意付费，也可能会对社会产生重大影响。

争议焦点：AI技术的隐私问题、用户接受度以及其是否会最终对社会产生积极影响。

The Force-Feeding of AI on an Unwilling Public
This isn't innovation, it's tyranny
Ted Gioia
Jul 05, 2025
1,205

The Honest Broker
The Force-Feeding of AI on an Unwilling Public
Copy link
Facebook

More
369
266
Share
A few months ago, I needed to send an email. But when I opened Microsoft Outlook, something had changed.
Microsoft asked me to use Copilot to write my email. Copilot is my AI
companion
. (That’s the cute word they use.)
Hey I don’t want a
companion
—especially not a fake AI buddy. I never asked for this.
And what about the people receiving my emails? They don’t want this either. They want to hear from me, not a bot.
How do I turn my
companion
off?
Please support my work by taking out a premium subscription—for just $6 per month (even less if you sign up for a year).
Subscribe
After some trial-and-error, I found a way to disable Copilot. Phew!
But a few days later, Microsoft surprised me again. It wouldn’t let me save an Excel file until I had agreed to new terms for my software account.
Guess what? AI is now bundled into
all
of my Microsoft software.
Even worse, Microsoft recently
raised the price of its subscriptions by $3 per month
to cover the additional AI benefits. I get to use my AI companion 60 times per month as part of the deal.
Source
But I don’t want to use it. I want to
kill
it.
As you can see, I’ve never used this service. I still have all 60 credits unused. But I’m paying for it—because it’s now embedded into Microsoft Word, Excel, etc.
This is how AI gets introduced to the marketplace—by force-feeding the public. And they’re doing this for a very good reason.
Most people won’t pay for AI voluntarily—just 8%
according to a recent survey
. So they need to bundle it with some other essential product.
You never get to decide.
Source
Before proceeding let me ask a simple question: Has there ever been a major innovation that helped society, but only 8% of the public would pay for it?
That’s never happened before in human history. Everybody wanted electricity in their homes. Everybody wanted a radio. Everybody wanted a phone. Everybody wanted a refrigerator. Everybody wanted a TV set. Everybody wanted the Internet.
They wanted it. They paid for it. They enjoyed it.
AI isn’t like that. People distrust it or even hate it—and more so with each passing month. So the purveyors must bundle it into current offerings, and force usage that way.
“That’s the blight of the AI revolution. It looks like spam. It smells like spam. It tastes like spam.”
There’s another reason why huge tech companies do this—but they don’t like to talk about it. If they bundle AI into other products and services, they can
hide the losses
on their income statement.
That wouldn’t be possible if they charged for AI as a standalone product. That would make its profitability (or, more likely, loss) very easy to measure.
Shareholders would complain. Stock prices would drop. Companies would be forced to address customer concerns.
But if AI is bundled into existing businesses, Silicon Valley CEOs can pretend that AI is a moneymaker, even if the public is lukewarm or hostile.
It’s like a restaurant selling granite rocks for dessert. Nobody will buy them or eat them—so the product fails miserably. But if a popular restaurant adds a dollar to the meal price, and gives every customer a rock with their bill—well, then they can say that:
Every customer gets rocks for dessert.
Every customer pays for it.
Their business is more profitable because of the tasty granite rocks.
This is how AI accounting works in Silicon Valley.
“The AI business model would collapse overnight if they needed consumer opt-in. Just pass that law, and see how quickly the bots disappear. ”
And that’s why Google does something similar to Microsoft. They add AI to search results—you don’t get to choose. It’s force-feeding all over again.
So these huge digital platforms can pretend that users have totally embraced the new tech.
Shut up, buddy, and chew on your rock
.
This is how AI gets implemented
everywhere
.
You don’t get to choose. You’re never asked. It just shows up. Now you have to deal with it.
I don’t want AI customer service—but I don’t get a choice.
I don’t want AI responses to my Google searches—but I don’t get a choice.
I don’t want AI integrated into my software—but I don’t get a choice.
I don’t want AI sending me emails—but I don’t get a choice.
I don’t want AI music on Spotify—but I don’t get a choice.
I don’t want AI books on Amazon—but I don’t get a choice.
If they gave people a choice, they would reject this tyranny masquerading as innovation.
The AI business model would collapse overnight if they needed consumer opt-in.
Just pass that law, and see how quickly the bots disappear.

data.title: Serving 200M requests per day with a CGI-bin
data.author: mustache_kimono
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了90年代的CGI技术在现代的应用潜力。作者回顾了自己在1990年代使用CGI进行网页开发的经历，并指出CGI为每个请求启动和终止进程的方式曾被认为效率低下，从而催生了如PHP和FastCGI等技术。然而，随着计算机性能的显著提升，使用Go和Rust等现代语言可以使CGI在当今环境下更高效。实验显示，在 modest 硬件上，CGI程序每秒可处理2400多个请求，每日可达2亿次请求。尽管作者不建议广泛采用这种方法，但认为在多核CPU环境下，CGI仍有其研究价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CGI技术的优缺点及其在现代web开发中的适用性

不同观点：
• Kragen认为，即使像Python这样的语言，CGI在当今仍然足够快。他指出，如果一个CGI脚本需要400毫秒的CPU启动时间，并且服务器有64个核心，那么每秒可以处理160个请求，每天可以处理1400万次点击。他批评了Python社区对稳定和向后兼容的技术持有负面态度，并指出CGI模块将在Python 3.13中被移除。

44476716.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Serving 200 million requests per day with a cgi-bin
(
via
) Jake Gold tests how well 90s-era CGI works today, using a Go + SQLite CGI program running on a 16-thread AMD 3700X.
Using CGI on modest hardware, it’s possible to serve 2400+ requests per second or 200M+ requests per day.
I got my start in web development with CGI back in the late 1990s - I was a huge fan of
NewsPro
, which was effectively a weblog system before anyone knew what a weblog was.
CGI works by starting, executing and terminating a process for every incoming request. The nascent web community quickly learned that this was a bad idea, and invented technologies like PHP and
FastCGI
to help avoid that extra overhead and keep code resident in-memory instead.
This lesson ended up baked into my brain, and I spent the next twenty years convinced that you should
never
execute a full process as part of serving a web page.
Of course, computers in those two decades got a
lot
faster. I finally overcame that twenty-year core belief in 2020, when
I built datasette-ripgrep
, a Datasette plugin that shells out to the lightning fast
ripgrep
CLI tool (written in Rust) to execute searches. It worked great!
As was
pointed out on Hacker News
, part of CGI's problem back then was that we were writing web scripts in languages like Perl, Python and Java which had not been designed for lightning fast startup speeds. Using Go and Rust today helps make CGI-style requests a whole lot more effective.
Jake notes that CGI-style request handling is actually a great way to take advantage of multiple CPU cores:
These days, we have servers with 384 CPU threads. Even a small VM can have 16 CPUs. The CPUs and memory are much faster as well.
Most importantly, CGI programs, because they run as separate processes, are excellent at taking advantage of many CPUs!
Maybe we should start coding web applications like it's 1998, albeit with Go and Rust!
To clarify, I don't think most people should do this. I just think it's interesting that it's not as bad an idea as it was ~25 years ago.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： humanoid机器人项目的技术、市场和伦理问题

不同观点：
• [技术可行性与挑战]  
  - [BrandiATMuhkuh] 提出关于双足机器人稳定性的质疑，认为双足设计不如四足稳定，且未见显著改进。  
  - [chrsw] 关注机器人足部设计，指出 humanoid 机器人缺少人类脚部的关键关节和感知能力，这可能影响其移动性能。  
  - [Mars008] 怀疑机器人的行走能力，认为即便在模拟器中训练，机械设计上的缺陷可能使其无法可靠行走。

• [市场定位与价格]  
  - [fragmede] 对比类似产品，质疑当前价格的合理性，认为额外费用未明确提供相应的增值功能。  
  - [srameshc] 关心 humanoid 机器人的实际用例，认为在当前阶段，购买这样昂贵的设备更像是一种投资而非消费。  
  - [deepdarkforest] 认为产品目前面向的消费者群体有限，对未来的市场前景持怀疑态度，并指出产品类似于特斯拉的FSD承诺，存在不确定性。  
  - [markisus] 提出该产品面临“寻找问题中的解决方案”的市场挑战，质疑其未来市场的潜力。  
  - [999900000999] 认为产品价格高昂，像是一种昂贵的玩具，并担心其可能被用于军事用途，带来伦理问题。

• [开源与社区贡献]  
  - [pj_mukh] 对开源软件部分感兴趣，询问具体的开放问题列表，但并未直接参与硬件投资。  
  - [randomNumber7] 质疑开源策略的有效性，认为控制系统的开发难度远高于硬件制造，并怀疑是否有人会贡献代码。  
  - [swyx] 分享团队工程师的幕后讨论，显示对项目技术进展的支持。

• [伦理与社会影响]  
  - [999900000999] 担心该技术可能被军事机构采用，并提出机器人拥有自由意志和道德问题的假设情境。  
  - [v5v3] 提到消费者市场对女性形象的机器人关注较多，并暗示这可能与孤独男性消费者市场相关。

补充讨论：
• [lachyg] 关注机器人手的设计，询问当前最佳的手部设计和未来合理价格的可能性。  
• [bbor] 表示对产品价格的认可，但指出链接404错误，提示技术文档的维护问题。  
• [dbmikus] 对团队在物理硬件、强化学习模拟环境和数据管理上的时间分配感兴趣，关注训练过程中的数据挑战。

争议焦点：
- 双足机器人设计的稳定性和实用性。
- 当前价格与功能之间的合理性。
- 开源策略能否吸引社区贡献代码。
- 机器人技术的伦理问题和社会影响。

主要讨论点：Morph工具的开发者体验（dev UX）、速度与质量的权衡、隐私问题以及与其他类似工具的比较。

不同观点：
• 关于速度与质量的优先级：
  - [deepdarkforest] 认为质量比速度更重要，尤其是在代码生成质量方面。即使编辑速度有200-300ms的差异，也不会成为开发者体验的瓶颈。
  - [elzbardico] 则以讽刺的口吻表示，开发者可能不得不面对大量AI生成的有问题的代码，暗示速度和质量同样重要。

• 功能性与使用场景：
  - [scottpersinger] 建议开发一个能智能合并代码的AI工具，认为这将显著提升开发速度。
  - [nico] 提出希望有一个浏览器扩展，可以连接ChatGPT和VSCode，从而实现代理编码。

• 工具性质与技术细节：
  - [Workaccount2] 询问Morph是否为整合其他LLM输出的工具，而不是一个LLM本身。
  - [simonw] 分享了使用Morph与Datasette工具集成的技术细节，但也提出了关于XML样式标签可能引起混淆的担忧。

• 隐私与数据使用：
  - [laborcontract] 对隐私政策表示关注，特别是付费用户的数据保留和使用问题，并询问是否可以选择不让数据用于模型训练。

• 与其他工具的比较：
  - [bijection] 询问Morph与Relace的比较，指出两者功能相似。
  - [seanw265] 询问Morph与其他模型（如Relace和Llama via Cerebras）在输出准确性上的比较。
  - [lastdong] 询问Morph是否类似于Gemini Diffusion。

补充讨论：
• [amelius] 建议可以让LLM直接输出patch文件，以简化代码更新流程。
• [handfuloflight] 询问如何将Morph引入Claude Code。
• [callamdelaney] 简单表示对该工具的需求。
• [rs186] 认为大公司可能很快会推出类似功能，并对Morph的API部分表示困惑，质疑开发者是否愿意将代码发送到另一个端点。

争议焦点：
• 速度与质量的优先级问题：一部分人认为质量更重要，而另一部分人则关注速度对开发体验的影响。
• 隐私问题：用户对数据使用和隐私政策的关注，特别是付费用户的数据处理方式。

这些观点反映了用户对Morph工具的功能、性能和隐私问题的多方面考虑，以及与其他类似工具的比较和竞争情况。
